data.delta:
## Executive Summary

Stripe remains one
of the most formidable private technology companies globally, positioning itself as the core
"financial infrastructure" layer for the internet. With 15,302 employees across
offices in San Francisco, Dublin, Seattle, London, Singapore, Tokyo, and more
, the company has scaled to serve millions of businesses—including an
estimated 62% of Fortune 500 companies. A reported ~$159B valuation (
per jobsbyculture.com) and a 2025 annual letter accompanied by a tender offer signal

the company is managing liquidity without a near-term IPO rush.

Strateg
ically, Stripe has made two significant M&A moves visible in the scraped data: the $
1.1B acquisition of Bridge Network (completed Feb 2025), its largest
deal ever focused on stablecoin/crypto payment rails, and the
acquisition of Orum (Jul 2025) to expand real-time, non-card payment infrastructure
. These moves indicate a deliberate push beyond card
-based payments into programmable money rails. Simultaneously, Stripe launched 288 products
at its "Sessions 2026" event and introduced an AI agent wallet—a signal that Stripe is racing
to own the machine-to-machine payments layer as a
gentic AI becomes mainstream. A May 2026 LinkedIn post confirmed: "Starting

today, you can set up machine payments with a single prompt to your agent."

Competitive positioning remains strong. Stripe
was named a Leader in the Forrester Wave™: Merchant Payment Providers, Q1 2026. Top competitors per
6sense data are PayPal, Adyen, and Venmo—but Stripe's developer-first model, breadth of recent

acquisitions, and AI-native product direction differentiate it meaningfully from these incumbents.

---

A massive thank you to Patrick Collison and John Collison for hosting me for their fireside chat to share the Speechify story at Stripe all-hands. What's always resonated with me about Patrick and John is how customer obsessed they've been since Day 1. There's the famous story of how during Y Combinator they would ask fellow founders to pull out their laptops and set up Stripe for payments right there on the spot. As they've grown to now thousands of teammates and millions of customers, that customer obsession remains. They're still hungry to know what can be improved. They invite customers to tell them what they need to work in front of the whole company. It's no surprise that in the AI era, they've remained the leader, helping support token-based business models that AI companies need to serve customers. As Speechify has evolved to serve professionals and companies in 200+ countries, paying with a wide set of currencies, Stripe has also made our global expansion as smooth as possible. We're lucky to have grown up with Stripe, to have expanded with Stripe, and to have entered the AI & now agent era with Stripe. Congrats Patrick, John, Jay Shah, Maia Josebachvili, and team for powering a staggering 1.6% of Global GDP. We're forever grateful. – Written with Speechify Voice Typing

Today, we're proud to announce that Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments by Amazon Web Services (AWS) is integrating Privy wallets. AI agents are starting to transact, not just reason and act. That shift requires payments to be built directly into how they operate. By combining AgentCore payments with Privy's embedded wallet infrastructure, this helps developers connect to their wallets for their agents, fund them (including via Stripe onramp), and define how they can spend—all within the same environment where agents are built and run. This helps developers to develop agentic payment solutions to pay for APIs, data, and services as part of their execution, without custom billing integrations or workflow interruptions. This builds on our work with agent wallets, including delegated signing—giving developers the tools to safely put money in motion for autonomous systems. Together with the Stripe Partner Ecosystem, we're excited to work with AWS to help define how payments integrate into the agent stack. Learn more 👉 https://lnkd.in/ePVrm6C8

assistant.question: Tell me what Bright Data products would best be used to research the company at stripe.com, and what data sources you would recommend for competitive intelligence on them.
assistant.answer:
{"answer":"Use these Bright Data products for Stripe research, in this order:

1. [Datasets](https://brightdata.com/cp/datasets/browse)  
   Best for pre-collected structured data you can use for competitive intelligence.

2. [Custom Scrapers](https://brightdata.com/cp/scrapers/request/create)  
   Best when you need Stripe-specific fields or sources that are not covered by an existing dataset.

3. [IDE](https://brightdata.com/cp/scrapers/automation/chat)  
   Best if you want to build and test your own scraping workflow.

4. [Web Unlocker](https://brightdata.com/cp/zones)  
   Best for accessing public web pages reliably when collecting Stripe-related source data.

For competitive intelligence on Stripe, collect public web data from these source types:

- Stripe’s own website and product pages
- Job postings and hiring pages
- Tech stack and infrastructure pages
- Blog posts, press releases, and changelogs
- Developer docs and API documentation
- Partner/integration directories
- Customer case studies and testimonials
- Review sites and app marketplaces
- Pricing and plan pages
- Public company profiles and news mentions
- Competitor websites for feature, pricing, and positioning comparison

For datasets, focus on:

- Company profiles
- Job listings
- Technology stack data
- App/review data
- B2B company datasets
- Public web content collections relevant to fintech and payments

No Stripe-specific Marketplace Dataset is currently listed, so a general public-web collection approach is the right fit.

Do you want to develop your own scraper or for us to develop it for you?

If you want, I can also help you choose between [Datasets](https://brightdata.com/cp/datasets/browse) and [Custom Scrapers](https://brightdata.com/cp/scrapers/request/create) for this use case.","dialog_id":"6a16e146f127c9ae539887d5"}
